content: RBM3, also known as Putative RNA-binding protein 3, is a protein encoded by the RBM3 gene in humans. This gene belongs to the glycine-rich RNA-binding protein family and encodes a protein that contains a single RNA recognition motif (RRM) domain. The expression of the RBM3 gene is upregulated in response to cold shock and hypoxic conditions (low oxygen tension). Additionally, a pseudogene corresponding to RBM3 is located on chromosome 1. Alternative transcriptional splicing of this gene results in the production of different isoforms, which have been characterized. RBM3 is a cold-inducible RNA-binding protein that plays a role in mRNA biogenesis and exhibits anti-apoptotic properties. Antibody-based profiling and transcriptomics analyses have demonstrated that RBM3 protein is expressed in all analyzed human tissues. Confocal microscopy studies have shown that RBM3 is predominantly localized to the nucleoplasm. Clinically, RBM3 is considered a proto-oncogene and is associated with tumor progression and metastasis. It is also regarded as a potential biomarker for cancer. Based on patient survival data, elevated levels of RBM3 protein in tumor cells serve as a favorable prognostic biomarker in colorectal cancer.
